overview: Alabama's 1st district is an open seat after redistricting, and it leans heavily Republican with a partisan vote index of R+17. Jerry Carl, the former incumbent of the old district, faces Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. Carl has raised over $1.1 million and holds a large cash advantage, with more than $500,000 in outside spending supporting him. Jones has raised under $100,000. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all point the same direction: this is a safely Republican seat, and Carl is the strong favorite to return to Congress.
